1: The SEDC-10-63+ is a transformer-type directional coupler
2: Current transformer: one turn in the line, N turns to node X. A current sample I/N flows into X
3: Voltage transformer: N turns across the line, one turn in series between X and CPL. It adds U/N
4: Both 50 Ω loads take the current sample at X. On the way to CPL the voltage winding adds U/N: CPL = Uₓ + U/N
5: Forward wave (U = Z0I): the current and voltage samples balance at X, so Uₓ = 0. The termination gets nothing, CPL gets U/N
6: Reverse wave (U = −Z0I): the current and its sample flip, so Uₓ = −U/N. At CPL: −U/N + U/N = 0
7: The internal termination absorbs this sample, not the reverse wave itself: that continues to IN
8: The turns ratio N sets the coupling: about −10 dB for the SEDC-10-63+; finite directivity lets a little of the reverse wave through
